claims.text: SPS between 900 °C and 1000 °C will trigger nanoscale secondary-phase precipitation in the Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co alloy.
The precipitate will be an oxygen-stabilized Ti-rich phase, such as TiO or a Ti-based Laves phase.
The secondary phase will form a percolating network at grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
The secondary-phase network will suppress long-range Mg and cation diffusion and retard Mg volatilization.
Diffusion suppression by the precipitates will prevent bulk decomposition and promote densification.
The precipitates will impede oxygen ingress and promote a stable, adherent passive film that improves oxidation and corrosion resistance.
The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co starting powder is a BCC solid solution.
The starting powder has a nanocrystalline grain size below 50 nm.
Oxygen impurities are introduced or entrained during mechanical alloying.
Sintering above 1000 °C causes significant Mg loss, porosity, and composition deviation.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient driving force for bulk formation and secondary-phase precipitation.
A short SPS duration of minutes will limit grain coarsening.
Dissolved Ti will react with milling-derived oxygen during SPS to form TiO precipitates.
Atomic-size mismatch may drive spinodal decomposition into a Ti-rich secondary phase.
Elevated-temperature Ti-O affinity overcomes sluggish diffusion and supplies the driving force for oxide precipitation.
The optimized bulk alloy will exceed 98% of theoretical density.
The optimized bulk alloy will have Vickers hardness above 600 HV.
The optimized alloy will have a corrosion current density at least one order of magnitude below that of samples sintered below 800 °C or above 1000 °C.
The final microstructure will be a fine-grained BCC matrix containing uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates.
If the milling-derived oxygen content is too low, the Ti-rich barrier phase will not nucleate and the resulting BCC matrix will have poor oxidation resistance.

contradictions.description: The proposed phase is called an intermetallic while TiO is simultaneously given as its principal example. TiO is an oxide, whereas a Laves phase is an intermetallic; these are chemically and structurally distinct mediator classes.
